.github/workflows/quality.yml:
name: Checks and Storybook

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      update_visual_baselines:
        description: Capture and commit Linux reference images on a review branch
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    if: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.update_visual_baselines) }}
    name: Build and regression checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit
      - run: npm run verify
      - name: Upload developer test evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: developer-test-evidence
          path: test-results/
      - name: Upload Storybook build
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: apps/figma-storybook/dist

  deploy:
    name: Publish Storybook
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    concurrency:
      group: pages
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Deploy Storybook
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  visual-baselines:
    name: Capture review-branch visual references
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.update_visual_baselines && github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npm run build:storybook
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test:developer -- --project chromium --update-snapshots
      - name: Commit reference images on this review branch
        env:
          REVIEW_BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          test "$REVIEW_BRANCH" != main
          git add tests/developer/visual.spec.ts-snapshots
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then exit 0; fi
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git commit -m 'Record Linux Chromium visual regression references'
          git push origin "HEAD:$REVIEW_BRANCH"
      - name: Upload reference review evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: visual-reference-review
          path: |
            tests/developer/visual.spec.ts-snapshots/
            test-results/
.github/workflows/release.yml:
name: Publish release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Version already recorded in package.json (for example 0.5.1)'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: publish-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
      - name: Check release version and refuse replacement
        run: |
          test "$GITHUB_REF" = refs/heads/main
          node --input-type=module -e "import fs from 'node:fs'; const p=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json')); if(!/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/.test(process.env.VERSION)||p.version!==process.env.VERSION) throw Error('Input version must match package.json');"
          if gh release view "v$VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'This release already exists. Publish a new version instead.'
            exit 1
          fi
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit
      - run: npm run verify
      - run: npm run release:pack
      - name: Publish exact verified commit and assets
        run: |
          gh release create "v$VERSION" releases/"$VERSION"/* \
            --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "Croma DS $VERSION" \
            --notes-file RELEASE-NOTES.md --latest

# Contributing to Croma DS

Use Node 22.12 or newer and npm. Clone the repository, run `npm ci`, then `npm run dev`.
Create a branch for a change and open a pull request against `main`.

## Component changes

1. Read the component's source evidence and the rules in `docs/FIGMA-DESIGN-HYGIENE.md`.
2. Update shared components in `packages/figma-ds/src` and shared tokens in `packages/figma-foundations`.
3. Add or update Storybook examples for the affected states, including dark surfaces and narrow widths.
4. Add a meaningful behavior regression when behavior changes. Keep original Figma components separate from prototype extensions.
5. Update the public example in `apps/figma-storybook/developer/examples.tsx`; API pages are generated from the exported TypeScript API. Keep imports public. Update the request adapter/fixtures when its service contract changes.
6. Run `npm run verify`. Include the affected stories, source basis, changes and actual checks in the pull request.

Do not use prototype-specific CSS to disguise a missing shared rule. Do not change original artwork bytes or assert visual acceptance from a passing build. Never add the raw Figma archive, credentials, personal files or the private extraction corpus to this repository.

## Accessibility, browsers and visual references

Install the test browsers with `npx playwright install chromium firefox webkit`. Developer adoption tests run the request, form, theme and accessibility scenarios in all three browsers; Chromium also checks all 66 API pages. Existing source/component regressions retain their documented scope.

Eight Linux Chromium image references cover dark/light compositions, the floating input and form dropdown at 320px and 1280px. They detect code regressions and are not Figma sign-off. For an intentional reference change, push a review branch, run Checks and Storybook with `update_visual_baselines=true` on that branch, inspect the committed PNG diff and rerun normal checks. Baseline capture refuses main and never deploys Storybook. Do not update references to hide an unexplained failure.

## Releases

Component changes and repository changes use semantic versions. A patch version can correct behavior or developer tooling without adding a component API. Update the root and all four workspace versions together, refresh `package-lock.json`, and update `CHANGELOG.md` and `RELEASE-NOTES.md` in the same pull request.

After the main branch passes checks, run **Actions → Publish release → Run workflow** with the matching version. The workflow rebuilds and tests, packages the exact commit, creates its version tag and publishes the packages, source, Storybook and checksums. Existing releases are never overwritten. The earlier 0.5.0 tag is the initial archive distribution checkpoint; 0.5.1 starts the source-backed developer repository releases.

Storybook deploys to GitHub Pages after checks pass on `main`. Pull requests run the same checks but do not replace the public Storybook. The existing shared 0.5.0 catalogue remains a frozen review reference until separately updated.

## Package registry

The release archives support ordinary `npm install` over HTTPS without signing in or downloading files manually. The package names resolve to `@croma/figma-ds` and `@croma/figma-foundations` inside the project.

These packages have not been published to npmjs.com. Publishing under `@croma` requires that scope's owner to grant access. Do not claim ownership of Croma's namespace or rename imports silently. An authorised npm account and confirmed namespace are needed before adding registry publishing. GitHub Packages also requires separate client authentication; it is not used for anonymous installation here.

# Croma design system

Reusable React components and foundations built from Croma's actual Figma DS, with separately documented prototype extensions.

[![Checks and Storybook](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/actions/workflows/quality.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/actions/workflows/quality.yml)

[Storybook](https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/) · [Releases](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Use in a prototype

Use React and React DOM 19. Install the two matching **0.6.0** packages directly; no ZIP download, GitHub login or npm registry login is required:

```sh
npm install --save-exact \
  https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases/download/v0.6.0/croma-figma-foundations-0.6.0.tgz \
  https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases/download/v0.6.0/croma-figma-ds-0.6.0.tgz
```

Import the four stylesheets once at the application entry:

```tsx
import '@croma/figma-foundations/fonts.css';
import '@croma/figma-foundations/tokens.css';
import '@croma/figma-foundations/typography.css';
import '@croma/figma-ds/styles.css';
import {PrototypeButton, CromaProvider} from '@croma/figma-ds';

export function App() {
  return (
    <CromaProvider theme="dark">
      <PrototypeButton>Continue</PrototypeButton>
    </CromaProvider>
  );
}
```

CromaProvider applies the complete document background, text, colour scheme and full-height region. Use `applyDocument={false}` for embedded regions. Explicit source Theme props override inheritance; fixed source artwork keeps its original presentation. Remove conflicting legacy body/component styles.

Start with [the hosted developer guide](https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/?path=/story/developers-start-here--installation), [component choices](https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/?path=/story/developers-start-here--choose-components) and the React API pages for all public component exports. Each API page includes a compiled React example, props and source links. [API and forms](https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/?path=/story/developers-api-and-forms--search-request) demonstrates mocked requests, cancellation, retry, validation and retained values.

Use the documented shared components and tokens, remove conflicting legacy styles, and theme dialogs and overlays too. Read [design hygiene](docs/FIGMA-DESIGN-HYGIENE.md) and [prototype extensions](docs/FIGMA-PROTOTYPE-EXTENSIONS.md) before applying the DS to an existing prototype. Pin both dependencies to the same release and commit your lockfile.

The names `@croma/figma-ds` and `@croma/figma-foundations` are the installed import names. They are not currently published to npmjs.com. The HTTPS command above is the supported distribution route.

## Develop the library

Use Node **22.12+** and npm. The editable source is directly in the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS.git
cd Croma-Existing-DS
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Storybook opens at `http://localhost:6020`. Run `npm run figma:dev` for the consumer prototype at `http://localhost:5182`.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Build the DS and start Storybook |
| `npm run build` | Build the components and consumer prototype |
| `npm run build:storybook` | Build the static catalogue |
| `npm run typecheck` | Check TypeScript after building the DS |
| `npm test` | Run consumer and component browser regressions against built apps |
| `npm run verify` | Build, typecheck, check source/package boundaries and run browser tests |
| `npm run release:pack` | Package a clean, already verified source commit |

Install Chromium before running browser tests: `npx playwright install chromium` (Linux CI uses `--with-deps`).

## Repository structure

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/figma-foundations` | Tokens, typography, Switzer and font notices |
| `packages/figma-ds/src` | React components, styles and source artwork |
| `packages/figma-ds/evidence` | Curated source values and acceptance records |
| `apps/figma-storybook` | Stories and documentation |
| `apps/figma-prototype` | Consumer examples and acceptance harness |
| `tests` | Behavior, composition and source checks |
| `docs` | Source limits and reusable design rules |
| `.github/workflows` | Checks, Storybook deployment and versioned releases |

## Review and release

Use a branch and pull request for component changes. Checks run on pull requests and main-branch changes. Successful main-branch checks deploy the current development catalogue to GitHub Pages. [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the component and release process.

Release **0.5.1** started source-backed developer releases. Release **0.6.0** adds self-service documentation, application theming, shared colour tokens and developer quality checks. The earlier 0.5.0 tag records the initial archive distribution; its editable source is the named source ZIP in that release's assets. Existing downloads stay unchanged. The [shared 0.5.0 review catalogue](https://croma-figma-ds.bombaydc-3738.chatgpt.site) remains available separately.

Original Figma specifications take priority. Prototype extensions have separate implementation contracts. Full-system visual acceptance remains incomplete; builds and passing tests do not establish stakeholder sign-off.

No blanket open-source licence is asserted. Croma branding, artwork and supplied fonts retain their existing rights and notices. The raw Figma archive, private extraction corpus and credentials are excluded.

# Croma React Storybook

The public developer guide is https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/?path=/story/developers-start-here--installation. It contains versioned GitHub installation, complete CromaProvider setup, component choices, public React API pages and request/form examples. No private Space login or local-machine path is required.

From the repository root, with Node 22.12+ and npm:

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:6020. Use `npm run build:storybook` to build and `npm run figma:preview-storybook` to serve the static build at http://localhost:6021. `npm run figma:dev` starts the consumer example at http://localhost:5182.

`npm run build:storybook` regenerates the API pages from the public TypeScript declarations and checked-in React examples. Update `developer/examples.tsx` for a public component change; `scripts/build-developer-docs.mjs` rejects a missing public component example. All examples are typechecked. The generated files are checked in so reviewers can inspect the exact release.

The Component theme toolbar controls inherited Theme; Preview background changes only the surrounding canvas. Explicit source variants and fixed artwork retain their original appearance. Every React API page includes its source/extension boundary and current visual-acceptance limit.

API and forms uses MSW for fictional same-origin HTTP responses. The application adapter owns requests, validation, retry and stable product identity; the DS package has no Express or pipeline dependency. Mock handlers are Storybook-only.

Run `npm run verify` for the release checks. See the [root README](../../README.md), [contribution guide](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and [source verification](../../docs/FIGMA-VERIFICATION.md) for current commands and boundaries. Historical acceptance records remain evidence of their dated checks; they are not current acceptance receipts. Full original-Figma visual acceptance remains incomplete.
